title.narrative: MFF - Transport Network Development Investment Program

description.narrative: The MFF comprises physical investments for upgrading road and rail infrastructure, and nonphysical investments for institutional capacity development including project preparation and implementation management, asset management, and sector-wide planning and governance.

description.narrative: Increased movement of goods and services and better connectivity for people and businesses

By 2022: Increased availability of inter-city freight and passenger services: Volumes of traffic along project roads increased by 30% from 2011 Achievement: 15 Progress/Status: Volumes of traffic along project roads was envisioned to be increased by 15% with the completion of 209.5 km roads.
However, due to the change in government in mid-August 2021 and as per ADB's approach paper “Afghanistan 2021 Situation: Proposed Approach and Next Steps”, ADB has paused its operations and is not allowed to follow up and request/verify information with the EA on suspended works. Data Source: Socioeconomic surveys

By 2022: Increased average intercity travel speed: On national highway network average speed increased from 35 kph in 2010 to at least 50 kph in program areas Achievement: 25 Progress/Status: 209.5 km was envisioned to be completed which should have contributed to the increased speed on national highway network average.
However, due to the change in government in mid-August 2021 and as per ADB's approach paper “Afghanistan 2021 Situation: Proposed Approach and Next Steps”, ADB has paused its operations and is not allowed to follow up and request/verify information with the EA on suspended works. Data Source: Traffic counts and surveys

By 2022: Increased connectivity: Percent of project areas connected to the regional highway network by paved roads increased to 90% from 70% in 2010 Achievement: 52 Progress/Status: A total of 404.5 km roads was envisioned to be constructed.
Under Tranche 1, the construction of 94.5 km road was completed, consisting of 40 km of Bagramy-Sapary road, 32 km of Jabul Saraj-Nijrab road, and 22.5 km of Faizabad-Baharak road.
Under Tranche 2, the construction of 115 km road was completed, consisting of 33 km of Sapary-Surkhrod road, 32 km of Char-e-Anjir-Gereshk road, and 50 km of Sharan-Angor Ada road.
Under Tranche 3, the construction of the 87 km of Yakawlang-Dari Suf road was at 66.8% when it was abruptly stopped due to the change in government in mid-August 2021.
Under Tranche 4, the construction of the 108 km of Baharak-Eshkashim road was at 76.01% when it was abruptly stopped due to the change in government in mid-August 2021. Data Source: MPW and MOTCA records

By 2022: Travel time to the nearest primary school, healthcare facility, or other essential service in target areas is decreased by 25% or 15 minutes from the existing average of 1 hour in 2011 Achievement: 50 Progress/Status: At least 10 minutes travel time was envisioned to be reduced from 1 hour to 50 minutes.
However, due to the change in government in mid-August 2021 and as per ADB's approach paper “Afghanistan 2021 Situation: Proposed Approach and Next Steps”, ADB has paused its operations and is not allowed to follow up and request/verify information with the EA on suspended works. Data Source: Railway inspection reports Baseline value: 1 hour
